threads.thread_goal: Align on overall seasonal theme, bundles, and campaign calendar.

messages.text:
Hi all, sharing a first rough idea for the seasonal promotion so we can react.

Theme proposal: 'Spring table and garden refresh' linking restaurant dishes, bakery breads and desserts, meat grills, and fresh plants.

Very draft bundles:
- Restaurant set menu that uses bakery bread and a meat special
- Take-home bundle: marinated meat + bakery side + suggestion for matching herbs or plants
- Coffee and cake from bakery with a small discount if the customer also buys a potted herb

Calendar idea for the 3 weeks:
- Week 1: focus on bakery and restaurant
- Week 2: focus on meat and grilling
- Week 3: focus on garden and gifts, still keeping food offers

This would become our base for T1 and feed into the special menu work in T4 and the concept doc A1.

Can you check if this direction works for your areas and what I am missing?

I like the 'spring table and garden refresh' idea, it connects well with what we can show at the meat counter.

For bundles, from meat side we can easily support:
- Grill pack: mixed skewers + garlic bread from bakery
- Roast pack: marinated roast + dessert suggestion from bakery

On the calendar, could we make weekends more grill-focused in all three weeks? That is when customers ask most about barbecues.

If we agree on this direction, I can start detailing the meat bundles for T1 and T10 so they fit into A1.

From my side this theme also works. It is simple to explain to customers.

For bakery links, since I worked there before, I suggest we include:
- Breakfast combo: pastries + coffee in restaurant + small discount on a herb plant
- Bread and meat pairing board in the restaurant menu for T4.

On the 3-week calendar, maybe we can define one key product focus per week per section in A1 so staff know what to push each day.

The theme fits very well with plants and garden.

For the garden corner I can align T5 with this by:
- Highlighting herbs and edible flowers as 'bring the restaurant home'
- Using signage that repeats the same spring table message as in A1

On bundles, I suggest we define at least:
- Herb trio + recipe card that mentions the restaurant dishes
- Small flowering plant as an add-on when customers buy the grill pack.

For the calendar, could we lock in:
- Week 1: herbs and table plants
- Week 2: balcony and outdoor plants
- Week 3: gifts and centrepieces

If we agree, I will reflect this in T1 and T5.

Thanks all, this helps.

I realise my first draft was a bit generic. Let me try to summarise what we have so far for T1 and A1:

Theme: 'Spring table and garden refresh' (food and plants together).

Cross-section bundles we seem to like:
- Grill pack: mixed skewers + garlic bread + optional herb plant
- Roast pack: marinated roast + dessert from bakery
- Breakfast combo: pastries + coffee in restaurant + herb plant discount
- Herb trio + recipe card linked to restaurant dishes.

Calendar refinement:
- All weekends: grill focus
- Week 1: bakery + restaurant + herbs
- Week 2: meat + balcony/outdoor
- Week 3: garden gifts + still some food bundles.

Can you confirm if this is accurate before we lock it as our main direction for D1?

Your summary matches what I had in mind.

One detail for meat: for the grill pack and roast pack we should define clear price points and maximum quantities per customer in T10 so we do not run into stock issues.

From my side, I am ok to confirm this theme and these bundles as our main direction for D1, as long as we keep the weekend grill focus in the calendar.

I agree with the summary and with confirming D1.

For the calendar (D2), could we also mark a 'garden highlight day' each week in A1? For example:
- Week 1: herbs day
- Week 2: balcony plants day
- Week 3: gift plants day

That way I can plan T5 and T3 scripts around those days and we can mention them in the restaurant menu T4 as well.

I am also fine with the theme and bundles for D1.

On the calendar for D2, I suggest we keep it simple for staff:
- Each week has one main focus per section
- Weekends always grill
- Garden highlight day as suggested.

If we put this clearly in A1 with a small table, it will be easier to explain during the mini-training later.

Ok, sounds like we are aligned on the theme and bundles.

For D1, I will record:
- Final theme: 'Spring table and garden refresh'
- Main cross-section bundles: grill pack, roast pack, breakfast combo, herb trio with recipe card, plus the garden add-on for grill packs.

On D2, I want to be sure about the exact 3-week calendar before I put it into A1. Here is a proposal:

Week 1
- Restaurant: breakfast combo and herb-linked dishes
- Bakery: pastries and breads for breakfast
- Meat: lighter cuts, some grill
- Garden: herbs and table plants (herbs day on Wednesday)

Week 2
- Restaurant: grill plates
- Bakery: garlic bread and sides
- Meat: strong grill focus
- Garden: balcony/outdoor plants (balcony day on Thursday)

Week 3
- Restaurant: roast and dessert focus
- Bakery: desserts
- Meat: roast and some grill for weekend
- Garden: gift plants and centrepieces (gifts day on Friday)

Can you confirm this so we can close D2?

This calendar works for meat.

Only small tweak: in Week 1 I would still keep a clear grill message for the weekend, even if the weekday focus is lighter cuts. We can note that in A1.

With that adjustment, I am ok to confirm D2.

Calendar looks good for garden as well.

I will plan T5 so that the displays and plant selection follow those weekly focuses and highlight days.

From my side, D2 can be considered agreed with the note from meat about weekend grill focus in all weeks.

I am aligned with the calendar and the tweak suggested by meat.

This structure will also help when we define the restaurant menu items in T4, because we can match dishes to the weekly focus.

So from my side D2 is confirmed.

Thanks all.

I will update A1 and T1 with:
- D1: final theme and bundles as summarised
- D2: 3-week calendar with weekly section focuses, weekend grill emphasis, and the three garden highlight days.

Next I will start drafting the restaurant special menu items for T4 based on this calendar and share a separate update.

threads.thread_goal: Define and agree on display layouts for bakery, meat, and garden corners.

messages.text:
Following the theme and calendar in A1 and T1, I have sketched display layouts for bakery and meat stands for T2 and some ideas that should also connect to the garden corner.

Meat stand proposal:
- Front: grill pack bundles with clear price tags
- Left side: roast pack with recipe suggestion
- Back: regular cuts, but with small tags pointing to the promotion
- Top rail: signage repeating the 'spring table and garden refresh' line

Bakery stand proposal:
- Front: garlic bread and sides for grill
- Right side: pastries for breakfast combo
- Small central crate: desserts linked to roast pack

I will upload photos into A5 once we agree on the structure.

Can you review and suggest adjustments, especially on how to make the link to the garden corner for T5?

Thanks for putting this together.

On the meat stand, I would add a small corner for sampling when we run the bakery upsell from T9, so customers can taste the garlic bread with the grill pack.

For bakery, maybe we should keep the breakfast pastries slightly separated from the grill sides so the message is not confusing.

Once we agree, we can document the final layout in A5 for D3.

I like the idea but I am not sure where we put the normal meat items that are not in the promotion. Do we hide them or mix them in?

Also, for the bakery stand, could we just put everything together so customers see all options at once? That might be easier to set up quickly.

Good questions.

For the regular meat items, I suggest we keep them on the back part of the stand, with smaller tags, so they are still visible but the front is clearly about the promotion. That way we respect the calendar in A1 but do not confuse regular shoppers.

On the bakery stand, if we put everything together it may be harder for staff to explain the bundles. I would keep three clear zones: grill sides, breakfast pastries, and desserts. We can still keep them close so setup is not too complex.

Let us see what the restaurant manager thinks before we finalise D3.

From the garden side, I can mirror your layout so the link is clear for T5 and A6.

Garden corner proposal:
- Front: herbs in small pots, with a sign saying 'Pair with your grill pack'
- Left: balcony plants, with a note about outdoor dinners
- Right: gift plants and centrepieces for the Week 3 focus
- Top: same 'spring table and garden refresh' line as your top rail.

If we align the colours and fonts in A5 and A6, customers will see it as one promotion even if the stands are in different areas.

I support your three-zone idea for the bakery stand; it will also make it easier to write scripts in T3.

Thanks for the detailed proposals.

I want to be sure we can set this up without slowing service, given our constraint on staff.

Questions:
- For the meat stand, can we keep the sampling corner from T9 only during peak promotion times, not all day?
- For the bakery stand, how many signs do we need so that staff can still move easily?

Once we are clear on that, I am comfortable moving towards D3 for the bakery and meat layouts and D4 for the garden link.

On sampling, I suggest we limit it to two slots per day, for example late morning and late afternoon, as part of T9. That way we can plan staff time and avoid overload.

For signage, maybe three main signs per stand are enough: one for the theme, one for the main bundle, and one for the cross-sell message. The rest can be small price tags.

If that works for you, I think we can confirm D3 and D4 based on the layouts described and document them in A5 and A6.

I agree with limiting sampling to two time slots per day and keeping three main signs.

To make D3 explicit:
- Meat stand: front grill pack, side roast pack, back regular items, small sampling corner used only in the two daily slots from T9.
- Bakery stand: three zones (grill sides, breakfast pastries, desserts) with one main sign each.

For D4, the garden corner will mirror the structure with herbs in front and the same theme line, as described in A6.

I will update A5 with final sketches and photos accordingly.

From garden side, I confirm D4 as you summarised.

I will detail T5 so that:
- Herbs are placed in front with clear links to grill and breakfast bundles
- Balcony and gift plants follow the weekly focus from A1
- A6 includes photos and a short setup checklist so staff can replicate the layout quickly.

This will also help when we train colleagues using A5 and A6.

Ok, then we will go with these layouts.

I will note in A5 and T2 that:
- D3: bakery and meat stands follow the three-zone structure with limited sampling slots and three main signs.
- D4: garden corner mirrors the theme and structure, with herbs in front and matching signage as per A6.

Please share the final photos for A5 and A6 by the end of the week so we can use them in the mini-training.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize cross-selling scripts, signage wording, and legal info.

messages.text:
I have drafted initial cross-selling scripts for T3 and sign texts for T11, based on the theme and bundles in A1.

Examples for A2:
1) Customer buying grill meat
- Staff: 'If you like grilling, we have a spring bundle with garlic bread from our bakery and fresh herbs to match your meat. Would you like to see it?'

2) Customer at bakery stand
- Staff: 'These breads are part of our spring table promotion. If you are planning a meal, we also have marinated meat and herb plants that go with them.'

3) Customer in garden corner
- Staff: 'These herbs are the same we use in our restaurant dishes this month. If you want to try them, we have a menu and take-home bundles with meat and bread.'

Sign text ideas for T11:
- Main sign: 'Spring table and garden refresh'
- Sub-line: 'Match your meal with fresh bread, quality meat, and living herbs'

For legal and pricing info, I will need confirmation from the restaurant manager before we finalise A2 and T11.

Please review the tone and suggest changes so we can move towards D5 and D6.

These scripts sound natural to me.

For the meat counter, I would add one more line for customers who seem in a hurry:
- 'We have a ready grill pack with bread and herbs included, so you do not need to think about sides.'

On signage, we should make sure the price and weight information for meat bundles is clear, but I will rely on the restaurant manager to confirm the exact wording for T11.

I like the idea but I am not sure how much detail we should give about the herbs. Should we list the names or just say 'fresh herbs'?

Also, for the sign sub-line, is it ok if we just say 'fresh bread and meat with herbs' to keep it shorter?

Good point.

For scripts, I suggest we keep it simple and say 'fresh herbs' unless the customer asks for details. For the garden corner, we can add the plant names on small labels.

For the sign sub-line, we need to keep it short but also clear. Maybe: 'Fresh bread, quality meat, and living herbs for your table'. That keeps the three elements without being too long.

We will still need the restaurant manager to confirm any mandatory legal wording for prices and allergens in T11.

From meat side, I like the scripts and the shorter sub-line you just proposed.

One more script idea for A2 when customers are at the meat counter but not yet thinking about the promotion:
- 'If you are planning a meal this week, we have a spring offer that combines this cut with bread and herbs, and you can also try a similar dish in our restaurant.'

This connects the counter, bakery, and restaurant in one sentence.

Once we lock the final set of scripts, we can print a small cheat sheet for staff.

Thanks for pulling this together.

On legal and pricing info for T11, we must ensure:
- All bundle prices are clearly shown with currency and unit (for meat, price per kg and per bundle)
- Any allergens for bakery items are visible near the products
- The sign does not promise anything we cannot deliver (for example, we should not say 'all herbs organic' unless that is true).

I will check with our store operations manager about any extra wording we must include, especially for meat labelling, and then confirm here before we close D5 and D6.

That makes sense.

To move us closer to D5, here is a proposed final set of scripts for A2 and T3:
- Grill meat customer: 'We have a spring grill pack with garlic bread and fresh herbs included. It saves you time on sides. Want to hear the details?'
- Bakery customer: 'These breads are part of our spring table promotion. If you are planning a meal, we also have marinated meat and herb plants that go with them.'
- Garden customer: 'These herbs are the same style we use in our restaurant dishes this month. If you want to taste them, we have a menu and take-home bundles with meat and bread.'
- Busy customer: 'We have a ready grill pack with bread and herbs, so you do not need to think about sides.'
- General cross-sell at any section: 'This month we are running a spring table and garden promotion that links the restaurant, bakery, meat, and plants. If you like, I can show you the bundle that fits what you are buying.'

If everyone is ok with these, we can mark D5 as agreed and I will format them into A2.

I am comfortable with these scripts for D5.

They are short enough to use during busy times and still explain the bundles.

For D6, once the restaurant manager confirms the legal wording, I think the main sign and sub-line you proposed are fine.

Agreed on the scripts for D5.

For signage D6, I suggest we keep the structure:
- Top: 'Spring table and garden refresh'
- Sub-line: 'Fresh bread, quality meat, and living herbs for your table'
- Bottom: clear price and weight info, plus any legal notes.

We just need the restaurant manager to confirm the exact legal lines after checking with operations.

I have checked with our store operations manager about the legal wording for T11.

We must include:
- For meat bundles: 'Price per kg' and 'Bundle price' clearly, plus storage advice like 'Keep refrigerated' near the stand.
- For bakery: allergen statement near the products, for example 'Contains gluten, milk, eggs' where relevant.
- For the main sign: a small line at the bottom saying 'Offers valid while stocks last. See in-store labels for full details.'

With this, I think we can confirm D6 using the structure you suggested.

I also confirm D5 with the scripts listed in A2.

Great, then I will finalise A2 and T3 with the agreed scripts and update T11 with:
- Main sign and sub-line
- Legal and pricing lines you listed

To summarise for D5 and D6:
- D5: final cross-selling scripts are the five examples we agreed, one page per section in A2.
- D6: final signage wording uses the theme line, sub-line, and mandatory legal info, with details per section in T11.

I will share the formatted guideline in A2 once done so we can use it in the mini-training.

threads.thread_goal: Set up waste control, stock rotation, and tracking routines.

messages.text:
I have drafted a simple daily checklist for T6 and a tracking sheet structure for T7, which will become A3 and A4.

Checklist A3 (per day):
- Bakery: check expiry dates on pastries and breads, move older items to front, note any items to markdown.
- Meat: check use-by dates on grill and roast packs, confirm cold chain, mark items to be sold first.
- Restaurant: check prep quantities vs bookings, plan use of bakery and meat items that are close to date.

Tracking sheet A4:
- Columns: date, section, key items sold (units and value), waste (units and value), notes.

My idea is that each section fills its own line daily, and I consolidate once a week.

Can you review and tell me if this is practical for your areas so we can define D7 on who fills what?

The structure looks good and not too heavy.

For meat, I suggest we add to A3:
- Check display time for items on the stand vs storage rules
- Note any items moved back to cold storage.

On A4, it would help if we have a separate line for grill packs and roast packs, since they are key for the promotion.

For D7, I propose that the meat counter lead on each shift fills the checklist and tracking line for meat.

I agree with the additions from meat.

One question: for markdowns, do we record them as waste in A4 or separately? Sometimes we reduce price and still sell the item.

Maybe we should have a 'markdown' column so we can see how much we saved from becoming waste.

From garden side, I can also use a light version of the checklist in A3 for plants that are part of T5, even if they are not food.

For example:
- Check plant condition and remove damaged items
- Rotate older stock to the front
- Decide on small discounts for plants that are not moving.

On A4, I can fill a line for garden promotions with sales and markdowns, so we see the full picture of the campaign, not only food.

For D7, I am happy to take responsibility for filling the garden line daily.

I understand the idea but I am not sure when exactly we should fill the checklist. Is it at opening, closing, or both?

Also, who will show us how to use the tracking sheet A4? I do not want to make mistakes with the numbers.

Good questions.

I suggest we fill the checklist A3 once per day, during a calm moment, for example mid-afternoon, so we can still react the same day if needed.

For A4, I will walk everyone through it during the mini-training in T8 and also leave a simple example line in the sheet.

On the markdown question from meat, I like the idea of a separate column so we can see what was saved from waste. I will add a 'markdown value' column to A4.

That works for me.

To make D7 concrete, here is a proposal for responsibilities:
- Meat: shift lead fills A3 meat section and A4 meat lines daily.
- Bakery: bakery lead fills A3 bakery section and A4 bakery lines daily.
- Restaurant: you fill A3 restaurant section and A4 restaurant lines daily.
- Garden: garden seller fills A3 garden section and A4 garden lines daily.

You then consolidate weekly for the mid-campaign review.

If everyone agrees, we can record this as D7.

I am ok with that split for D7.

For meat, I will make sure the shift leads know they are responsible for both the checklist and the tracking lines.

The markdown column in A4 will also help us show how we avoided waste when we do the final report A8.

I agree with the responsibilities for D7.

For garden, I will add a small note in T5 so that the daily plant check is part of the routine, and I will fill A4 for garden each day.

This will give us a full view of sales and waste across all sections when we look at A4 during the campaign.

Ok, then we will go with this.

To summarise D7:
- Each section fills its part of A3 and A4 once per day, mid-afternoon.
- Meat, bakery, restaurant, and garden each have a clear owner as you listed.
- I will consolidate A4 weekly and share a short update in the channel.

I will update T6 and T7 with these responsibilities and add the markdown column to A4.

threads.thread_goal: Plan launch mini-training and define success review approach.

messages.text:
We are getting close to launch, so I want to align on the mini-training and how we will review results.

For T8 and A7, here is a draft agenda for a 30-minute huddle:
1) Theme and calendar overview (A1)
2) Displays: bakery, meat, garden layouts (A5, A6)
3) Scripts and signage: key phrases and legal info (A2, T11)
4) Waste and tracking routines: checklist A3 and sheet A4

I propose we run this the day before the promotion starts, at 15:00, when the store is usually calmer.

For the end-of-campaign review T12 and A8, my idea is:
- Use A4 to compare sales and waste per week
- Collect quick feedback from each section on what worked and what did not
- List 3–5 ideas for next season.

Please tell me if the timing and topics work for you so we can agree on D8.

The agenda looks complete.

For meat, 15:00 the day before works, but we should keep it tight so we can get back to prep.

I suggest we:
- Use printed versions of A5 and A2 so staff can take notes
- Do a quick walk to the stands after the huddle to check the layouts.

For the review T12, it would help if we agree now that each section brings one success and one issue to the final meeting, based on A4 and their experience.

I can attend at 15:00 and I like the idea of a short walk to the stands.

Could we also include a quick role-play of one or two scripts from A2, so staff feel more comfortable using them with customers?

From garden side, 15:00 the day before is also fine.

I support adding a short role-play segment. We can pair people from different sections so they practice cross-selling between food and plants.

For the review T12 and A8, I suggest we:
- Look at A4 by week and by bundle type (grill, roast, breakfast, herbs)
- Note any days where stock or weather affected results, so we do not misread the data.

This will make A8 more useful for planning next season.

I can join at 15:00, but I might need to leave a bit early if the counter gets busy.

Will the training cover exactly how to fill A4? I want to be sure I understand the numbers part.

Yes, we will cover A4 step by step in the training and I will show an example line.

Based on your feedback, I propose we adjust the T8 agenda in A7 to:
1) Theme and calendar (5 min)
2) Displays walk-through with A5 and A6 (10 min)
3) Scripts and quick role-play using A2 (10 min)
4) Waste checklist A3 and tracking sheet A4 (5 min)

We will keep it to 30 minutes and then do a short walk to the stands for anyone who can stay.

For the review T12, we will:
- Use A4 to look at sales, waste, and markdowns by week and bundle
- Each section brings one success and one issue
- Capture 3–5 improvement ideas in A8.

If this works, we can confirm D8 with this plan.

This agenda and review approach work for me for D8.

I will make sure meat staff attend the huddle and bring one success and one issue to the final review based on A4.

I confirm D8 from garden side.

I will prepare a short part in the training to show the garden corner layout from A6 and how to link plants in the scripts from A2.

For the final review T12, I will bring notes on which plant types worked best with each bundle so we can include that in A8.

I am aligned with D8.

The role-play and the clear structure will help staff remember the key points during the campaign.

I will also note any customer comments about the bundles so we can share them in the final review for A8.

Thanks everyone.

To close D8:
- Training: 30-minute huddle at 15:00 the day before launch, with the four agenda points we listed, using A1, A5, A6, A2, A3, and A4, plus a short walk to the stands.
- Attendees: key staff from restaurant, bakery, meat, and garden; I will track attendance in A7.
- Final review: after the 3 weeks, we meet using A4 and notes from each section to complete T12 and produce A8 with results and 3–5 improvement ideas.

I will update T8 and T12 accordingly.
